description: A one-voice player for the .wav files in a folder on disk, with a recorder for capturing a new one into the same list

params.text: Chooses which of the loaded .wav files plays, sweeping the whole folder from the first file at the left to the last at the right
Shifts the playback speed, marked in semitones and running ±24 semitones; 0 plays the file at its written pitch
Sets the rise time of the amplitude envelope, 1ms at the left and 1 second at the centre; at the far right the rise never completes and nothing is heard. With Hold / Decay chosen it sets a hold time
Sets the fall time of the amplitude envelope, 1ms at the left and 1 second at the centre; at the far right the level holds and the sample plays through without fading
Sets where playback begins, 0 to 100 per cent of the sample's length; for a sample under 2 seconds the knob is squared, giving finer control near the start
Sets where playback ends, 0 to 100 per cent of the sample's length; set below START and the sample is read backwards
Opens a file browser; pick any file and every .wav file in that folder is read into memory, up to 256 of them
Turns looping on and off: with it on the sample jumps back to START each time it reaches END instead of stopping
Starts the sample from its START position; pressing it again restarts from there. It does nothing until a sample is loaded
Starts recording what arrives at IN, and a second press stops it; the press is ignored unless IN is patched

inputs.text: Added to the SAMPLE knob at 10% of the folder per volt, moving the choice of file
Added to the TUNE knob at one volt per octave of playback speed, with the total held between -4 and +4 octaves
Added to the ATTACK knob at 10% of its travel per volt
Added to the DECAY knob at 10% of its travel per volt
Added to the START knob at 10% of the sample per volt
Added to the END knob at 10% of the sample per volt
The signal recorded into the current slot, read as ±5V and clipped there
A pulse here starts recording, and the next pulse stops it; it is ignored unless IN is patched
A pulse here starts the sample from its START position

outputs.text: A 1ms pulse at 10V each time playback reaches the END position, whether it then loops or stops
The sample, scaled to ±5V and shaped by the attack and decay envelope; 0V while nothing is playing

notes: nothing plays until a folder is loaded: click LOAD and pick any file, and every .wav file beside it is read in.
only the first channel of each .wav file is read, so a stereo file plays as its left channel alone.
pressing REC moves the SAMPLE knob to the far right and records into a new slot after the last loaded file.
a recording stops on its own after 441000 samples, which is 10 seconds at a 44.1kHz engine rate and shorter at a higher one.
a file whose own sample rate differs from the engine rate is corrected as it plays, so it sounds at its written pitch.
the screen draws the sample's name, its number in the folder, its waveform, the START and END markers and the play position. It is a drawing only, and nothing on it can be clicked or dragged.
menu: Envelope: Attack / Decay, Hold / Decay — chooses whether the ATTACK knob sets a rise time or a time the envelope holds at full level before the decay
Interpolation: None, Linear, Hermite, BSPLine — sets how a value between two stored samples is worked out when TUNE moves playback off the file's own rate
Slice mode — quantises START and END to sixteenths of the sample and draws the division marks on the screen
Low cpu mode — nothing in the module reads this setting and it is not written into the patch, so turning it on changes nothing
Trim sample — shortens the sample in memory to the section between START and END; with START above 0 the copy runs past the end of its own buffer, so the result cannot be relied on
Save sample — writes the sample in memory into the loaded folder as a new 32-bit mono .wav file
